openings.claim: The shared-tray organization may manufacture demand for corrective checking: competing reaches interrupt picking, shared items are omitted, and checking only after stacking leaves that arrangement operating throughout the batch. This proposed feedback path is unproven; the records are synthetic stipulations.
openings.delta: Reverse the assumption that tray organization merely answers an accuracy problem: centralized access may help cause it. Remove shared access for a bounded comparison while preserving each pattern's exact contents and the participants' complete-kit outcome.
openings.prediction: With the same pattern mixture, volunteer assignments and checking procedure, temporarily staging specified materials beside each volunteer will reduce crossing reaches and shared-material omissions together, reducing correction work.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is confusion about differing pattern quantities, independent of shared access. Local staging would reduce crossing reaches but omissions would persist for the same patterns; O4 could reflect an easier pattern mixture.
openings.defeat: Matched blocks show fewer crossing reaches under local staging but unchanged or increased shared-material omissions. That dissociation would defeat the proposed interruption-to-omission explanation.
openings.probe: Within the actual 60-kit workload, compare two matched six-kit blocks with identical pattern counts, alternating which volunteer starts with each arrangement. Use existing trays, supplies and tally sheets; retain specified quantities and dimensions. Record crossings, omissions, assembly and checking time. First check that staging fits entirely on the table and that comparison plus remaining assembly and checking can fit the two-volunteer 90-minute budget; if either fails, do not run this probe.
assumptions: Matched pattern blocks can be allocated within the required 60 kits.
Existing trays can stage local materials without overflowing the table; available area is unconfirmed.
The bounded comparison and all required checking can fit within 90 minutes; O4 does not establish full-batch capability.
This evaluates the bounded probe, not a proven full-batch intervention or demonstrated benefit.
